items.title: The most valuable part of an agent prompt is the list of things it refuses to do
items.pt:

items.title: Snow White is Actually a Story About Burnout, Cobalt Mining, and Legacy Code
items.pt:
Forget Disney. You are living in the Dwarf Barracks.


We’ve been reading the wrong documentation for centuries. 

We thought Snow White was a charming medieval bedtime story. In reality, it is a hardcore system post-mortem detailing the toxic reality of late-stage tech capitalism, zero-day exploits, and physical infrastructure exploitation.

If you peel back the fairytale varnish, the architecture is terrifyingly familiar:



The Magic Mirror? A multimodal LLM trained on toxic engagement metric

items.title: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay
items.pt: Modern video games provide a measurable testbed for AI models, combining abilities of visual understanding, instruction decomposition, goal planning, and precise action control over multiple temporal horizons. items.title: VideoGen-Agent: Reinforcing Video Generation Agents
items.pt: Recent advances in video generative models have enabled high-fidelity, temporally coherent video generation. items.title: onPanda: Efficient Annotation of On-Policy Alignment Data for LLMs and Agents via Token-Level Correction
items.pt: We present onPanda, an interactive tool for efficiently annotating LLM alignment data and agent trajectories. onPanda adopts token-level correction as its core interaction: while reading a model response, the annotator locates the first inappropriate token and either picks a substitute from the model's candidate tokens or types the correct text via free-form editing. The system then truncates everything after that position and continues generation from the corrected prefix, repeating this locate

items.title: LoRA-generating hypernetworks for efficient on-device LLM generative personalization
items.pt: On-device large language models (`LLMs'), e.g. running on mobile phones, are ripe for improvement via personalization. The limited compute resources of mobile devices impose limits on model scale and thus model quality, making any realizable quality gains highly impactful. At the same time, their personal nature (i.e., the close coupling to a particular user) means that a given on-device LLM tends to be used in similar, predictable patterns over the course of time.
